items.title: Michael White interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 10, 2025
items.q: He reminded me of middle-period Miles Davis in that sense in that he would leave a lot of spaces.

ctx.x: And don’t forget about the rests.

Yes. Space is very important as well. Because the music has to breathe. Even if the rhythm plays and there’s nothing quite going on right there, if it’s breathing in part of the rhythm it can be great. One of the interesting players I played with was Kid Thomas Valentine, who was a trumpet player. He was born in 1896, before Louis Armstrong. And he had his own kind of style, big beautiful, expressive tone. But he was what I would call a minimalist. He reminded me of middle-period Miles Davis in that sense in that…
This has really been a fascinating conversation, we could do a part two and part three. What’s next up for you? Are you going to go compose after we’re done here?
